key_insight: Routing-aware pruning removes two-qubit gates only when their expected fidelity cost is lower than the cost of executing them, and this criterion works across both NISQ and fault-tolerant quantum architectures.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a compilation-level way to reduce circuit depth, routing overhead, and error exposure without changing the target algorithm, making it useful for near-term hardware and future FTQC stacks.
method: Estimate an architecture-independent lower bound for the fidelity loss caused by omitting each parametric two-qubit gate.
Compare that bound against a hardware-specific routing execution cost model for the given architecture.
Prune gates whose computational benefit does not justify their execution cost, with an analytical boundary based on rotation angle, qubit distance, and noise.
evidence_signal: Benchmark simulations report up to 48.6% fewer gates and up to 47.7% higher fidelity in the NISQ regime, while FTQC analysis suggests pruning remains useful across multiple code distances and physical error rates.
watch_item: Pruning decisions depend on the accuracy of the routing and noise models, so miscalibration could cause overly aggressive gate removal or missed optimization opportunities.
paper_title: Quantum Circuit Pruning: From NISQ Architectures to Fault-Tolerant Operations
